question.prompt:
A regular octagon \(ABCDEFGH\) has an area of one square unit. What is the area of the rectangle \(ABEF?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_12B_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Joining the octagon's center to its vertices divides it into eight congruent triangles. This makes it possible to compare areas while leaving the side length unknown.

Let \(s>0\) be the side length and let \(a>0\) be the perpendicular distance from the center to a side, called the apothem. Each central triangle has base \(s\) and height \(a\). The eight triangles fill the octagon without overlapping interiors, so
\[
1=8\left(\frac12sa\right)=4sa.
\]
The sides \(AB\) and \(EF\) are opposite sides of the regular octagon. A half-turn about the center exchanges them, so they are parallel and lie at distance \(a\) on opposite sides of the center. Their separation is therefore \(2a\).

Rectangle \(ABEF\) consequently has dimensions \(s\) and \(2a\), giving area
\[
s(2a)=2sa=\frac12(4sa)=\boxed{\frac12}
\]
square unit, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Compare areas using the center
